script: I finally had enough. I got my primary Gmail account back when it was invite‑only—so I've had it forever, firstname.lastname@gmail, the kind of address that looks super legit. Over the years, I found two things. First, I share a name with an indie director. Second, I share a name with a bunch of people who don't even know their own email address. Like, someone in Ireland, I am in Canada, bought stuff and I got the receipt with the full identity‑theft starter pack. And there's this sales critter in the Chicago area who's as dumb as a sack of hammers. The Chicago guy is the real drama. He had a job, but was hunting elsewhere. So, he kept copying himself on every submission. The full identity kit, premium style, all the info. I sent "Wrong email." then "Wrong email again." then "Wrong email, check it." Some were hostile at first, but finally they had to admit they'd messed up. I still get misdirected emails for the director, and I politely say, "Wrong email, good luck with your project!" (I know, right?) But wait—this guy in Chicago keeps sending group emails. It reached a breaking point tonight. There's a golf outing email that keeps blasting after I told them "Wrong person. Check the emails." It's like a relentless spam bot. So I sent one more. "Still the wrong <my name> as I have told you before. If you see <my name> at the outing, please tell him thank you for the free <to me> porn. I wonder about his tastes." I am waiting for the follow‑up shitshow with glee. (Literally insane.) Then it hit me—his reply is probably going to be a meme. The next email is coming. I am ready.
